samples.summary: The design doc still records the removed contract: `spec-to-pr.mjs review` "needs CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN and degrades to a warn-and-skip when it is absent"
samples.evidence: docs/design/harness-engineering.md:2403-2406 (Phase 25 bullet) says: "**Local review is a convenience, not authority:** `spec-to-pr.mjs review` runs the same lenses over the working diff, but needs `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` and degrades to a warn-and-skip when it is absent." This diff deletes exactly that early return (`cmdReview` now emits `ambientAuthNotice` and proceeds on the logged-in session, scripts/agent/spec-to-pr.mjs:265) and makes the local round a real billed multi-lens run. `docs/design/agentic-dev-loop.md:57,79` and `.claude/commands/spec-to-pr.md` were updated on this branch; this consumer was not, so the repo now documents both contracts. The backticked-path CI check only resolves paths, so nothing mechanical catches the stale prose.

samples.summary: A blocking finding with no `file` is printed with `(no file cited)` and a `?`-filed key, but the out-of-diff rebuttal matcher gates on exact `file` equality, so such a finding can never be disputed through `--rebuttals`
samples.evidence: `renderBlockingFindings` (scripts/agent/spec-to-pr.mjs:338) renders a file-less finding as `(no file cited)` and its key via `findingKeyOf`, which substitutes `"?"` for a missing file (scripts/agent/rebuttal.mjs:276). The panel's matcher is `findingSimilarity`, which returns 0 unless `trimmed(a.file) === trimmed(b.file)` (scripts/agent/rounds.mjs:522), reached from `matchRebuttal` (scripts/agent/rebuttal.mjs:315,324). `.claude/commands/self-review.md` tells the developer to copy the printed `lens`, `file` and `summary` into the record — copying `(no file cited)` or `?` yields no match, and `review-panel.mjs` treats an unmatched rebuttal as no rebuttal, so the dispute is silently unheard and the finding is re-raised every round until `--force`. This is the same silent-no-op class the new `normalizeRebuttals` was added to close; the file-less case is left open.

samples.summary: The agent-track `spec-to-pr` flow is another caller of `review`, and it now hard-fails where it previously warned and continued — its instructions say nothing about the new round bound or a credential failure
samples.evidence: .claude/commands/spec-to-pr.md step 6 runs `node ./scripts/agent/spec-to-pr.mjs review` as a step before step 7 (VERIFY) and handoff. Before this change a machine with no token printed a warning and returned, so the flow always reached step 7. Now the panel always runs and any credential/SDK failure exits 1 through `fail("local review panel failed: …")` (scripts/agent/spec-to-pr.mjs:1099), and a fourth round on the same branch is refused outright by `roundBoundNotice` unless `--force` is passed. The command text this diff rewrites tells the agent to "re-run" but never mentions `--force`/`--fresh` or what to do when the round cannot run, so an agent driving that flow can be stopped before handoff with no documented next step (contrast `.claude/commands/self-review.md`, which does cover both).

samples.summary: The `3`-round bound is restated as prose in three docs while `MAX_SELF_REVIEW_ROUNDS` is the enforcing constant — a duplicated constant with nothing tying the copies to it
samples.evidence: `MAX_SELF_REVIEW_ROUNDS = 3` (scripts/agent/spec-to-pr.mjs) is what `roundBoundNotice`/`cmdReview` enforce, while CLAUDE.md:65 ("max 3 rounds"), CONTRIBUTING.md:184 ("at most **3 rounds**") and .claude/commands/self-review.md ("Bounded at **3 rounds**", plus the three-row lens table) each hard-code the number independently. Changing the constant leaves all three copies wrong and no lane checks prose against it; the drift guard added in prior-findings.test.mjs covers only the workflow's inline projection.

searchedFor: grep parseRebuttalComment / matchRebuttal / findingSimilarity in scripts/agent
read review-panel.mjs:2661-2670 (--rebuttals reader: only object-shape filtering)
finding.summary: The new local `--rebuttals` path reproduces only ONE of `parseRebuttalComment`'s normalizations, so a hand-written record missing `lens` or `file` is accepted and then silently adjudicates nothing
finding.evidence: `normalizeRebuttals` (scripts/agent/spec-to-pr.mjs, the `.map((r) => ... replace(/^agent-review-/, ""))` helper) only strips the check-run prefix and drops non-objects; `readRebuttalRecords`/`prepareRoundInputs` then write the records straight to the panel's `--rebuttals`. The cloud channel goes through scripts/agent/rebuttal.mjs:203-205, which REFUSES a record whose `lens` or `file` is empty (`if (lens === "" || file === "") return null;`) precisely because "without both, a rebuttal can never match anything". The consumers confirm it: scripts/agent/rounds.mjs:521-522 returns 0 unless `lens` AND `file` compare equal, and scripts/agent/review-panel.mjs:2328-2330 partitions with `(typeof r?.lens === "string" ? r.lens : "") === lensId`, where `lensId: lens.id` (review-panel.mjs:3018) is always non-empty. So a developer following .claude/commands/self-review.md who omits `file` (or spells the path differently from the finding's) gets a run that prints "adjudicating 1 rebuttal(s)" and adjudicates none — the silent-loss failure the docblock above `normalizeRebuttals` calls "the worst failure this path has". Fix belongs on the new code: mirror rebuttal.mjs:203-205's non-empty lens/file rejection, not only its prefix strip.

verdict.reason: I could find no non-empty lens/file validation anywhere on the local `--rebuttals` path. `normalizeRebuttals` (spec-to-pr.mjs:632-636) only drops non-objects and strips the `agent-review-` prefix; `readRebuttalRecords` (:663-673) rejects only missing file, unparseable JSON, and zero records — and spec-to-pr.test.mjs:503 explicitly pins that `{claim:"x"}` (no lens, no file) survives. Those records are written to the round's rebuttals.json (:686-688) and passed to the panel (:713), whose own reader (review-panel.mjs:2664-2665) filters object shape only. Downstream, review-panel.mjs:2328-2331 partitions on `r.lens === lensId` (lensId = lens.id, :3018) and returns an all-zero tally when nothing matches, while rounds.mjs:521-522 returns 0 unless both lens AND file compare equal — so a record missing either is dropped. The drop is silent: the only adjudication log is gated on `tally.matched > 0` (review-panel.mjs:3021), and I found no unmatched-rebuttal warning in rounds.mjs or panel-round-comment.mjs, while spec-to-pr.mjs:1062 has already printed "adjudicating N rebuttal(s)". The cloud channel does enforce this (rebuttal.mjs:203-205, rationale at :183-185), confirming the invariant the downstream consumers assume. In lane for blast-radius: an invariant other modules rely on, violated where those modules read it; major (a dispute is reported as heard and silently skipped).
